scope: Twenty additional AP Macro conceptual items: keys, distractors, assumptions and counterexamples. First substantive self-review, not independent review or empirical validation.

findings.macro-capital-deepening: Hold all other production determinants fixed, not only technology.

entries.reasoning: Fixed resources and technology preserve the feasible set. Using idle resources can move an interior bundle toward its boundary without an outward shift; the question asks possibility, not guaranteed attainment.

At two cloth per grain, the low-cost producer receives exactly its forgone cloth per exported grain, so has zero strict marginal gain. The other producer can gain. Constant opportunity costs and the basic trade model support the endpoint conclusion.

The previously produced car is excluded from current production. The separately supplied current brokerage service counts. Neither the entire resale price nor the old manufacturing cost belongs in current GDP.
An unrequited transfer is not government purchases in expenditure GDP. Subsequent spending may buy current output but is a separate transaction, preventing double counting.
New domestic final output is included when produced through inventory investment. Sale in a later period reduces inventories as expenditure rises; the original output is not produced again.

Imported basket goods enter consumer purchases but not domestic production. The question asks a direct price effect and says the deflator need not rise, rather than excluding all possible indirect effects.
For employed E>0 and unemployed U>=1, (U-1)/(E+U-1)<U/(E+U). Explicit positive employment prevents equality in the all-unemployed boundary case. Leaving active search creates no new job.

Potential output in the standard model corresponds to zero cyclical unemployment, not zero search or mismatch. The word can avoids asserting positive frictional and structural unemployment in every conceivable economy.

The existing nominal repayment is fixed. A higher realized price level reduces its purchasing power relative to expectation, favoring the borrower and hurting the lender on this repayment dimension; other things equal excludes offsetting positions.
Under existing progressive taxes, a decline in pretax income lowers tax payments without new legislation, cushioning disposable income and induced demand. No claim of complete stabilization follows.

With AD fixed and nominal wages/input prices falling, costs at each output decline and SRAS shifts right in the stated self-correcting model. Productive capacity need not change. The explanation acknowledges the model does not establish adjustment speed.
A valuable illiquid real asset is wealth but lacks general acceptability as a direct medium of exchange. Possible isolated barter does not make a house generally accepted money.

Discounting unchanged positive promised payments at higher market yields lowers present value. Holding risk and maturity comparable avoids treating a coupon reset or changed credit quality as the experiment.

Reserve balances are bank assets; equity is assets less liabilities. Deposits are liabilities, not equity. Settlement use and loss absorption are different functions, although both can constrain operations.

In the standard fixed-supply money market, higher nominal transactions shift money demand right, raising the clearing nominal rate. The item explicitly limits the conclusion to that framework rather than an administered-rate operating system.

With adjusted inflation expectations, an anticipated permanent inflation difference does not maintain a negative unemployment gap in the stated model. The explanation allows the natural rate itself to change.

For y=f(k), f prime positive and f double-prime negative imply increasing output per worker with decreasing increments. Added an explicit all-other-production-determinants-fixed condition, since technology alone does not rule out changes in human capital or other inputs.

Foreign currency per domestic unit times domestic prices converts domestic goods to foreign-currency prices. Dividing by foreign prices gives relative cost eP/P*. With e and P* fixed, an increase in P is real appreciation under this stated convention.

Under the stated accounting simplifications CA=S-I, so I>S implies a deficit. Neither negative saving nor any equality of gross and net exports follows. Net primary income/transfers may distinguish CA from net exports.

A rise in quoted interest with materially higher default risk does not identify the sign of the change in risk-adjusted expected return. Neither unconditional inflows nor unconditional outflows are warranted.
